s10.old: - **Scenario protocol: always run baseline + perturbed at the SAME seed, so deltas are exact with zero MC noise.** Residual cross-seed variance (about $13M between seed99/199 at MC = 20) is baseline-credibility only (which seed picked), irrelevant to same-seed deltas; bump MC or seed-ensemble later if the baseline itself needs to be less arbitrary. `per_topic_flip` is already deterministic (greedy LT, no MC).

s10.old: - `defection(m,dlean)`: if |dlean| >= DTHRESH = 15 and the member is persuadable (NOT Champion/Defender/Opponent), drag stance toward the money by int(|dlean|/DTHRESH) tiers along ORDER. comp + $250k defects Ally to Neutral etc. Dials MAXSHIFT = 40, HALF = 0.10, DTHRESH = 15 (as of this step; MAXSHIFT later 18 per calibration; the calibration note records DTHRESH 25 to 15, a discrepancy with this step's DTHRESH = 15 that the sources do not reconcile).

s10.old: - **HONEST LIMITATIONS**: (1) CU spends only act via conversion/defection, no gradual winnability in the coalition cascade (that is the FLIP model); a non-converting CU spend shows about 0 effect. (2) 18 low-receipt floor members (incl Grijalva) defect too easily (the receipts-floor artifact). (3) The runner is ONE-SHOT (apply then observe); the ADAPTIVE optimizer (Golovin-Krause: greedily CHOOSE the moves to max influence under budget, observing realized defections) is the natural next layer, NOT built at that point.
s10.why: "the natural next layer" is the next development step, not a place in the note

s10.old: - **H2 (FIXED)**: scenario per-topic rows were below the MC noise floor (std about 0.75-1.05 vs 0.3 threshold), giving impossible "competitor money helped CU" signs. Root cause: the cascade drew `random.random()` in activation order, so changing one member desynced the whole stream (CRN failure). Fix: splitmix64 `_sm(it,u,v)` edge-keyed draws = true CRN, so baseline vs scenario differ ONLY by the real perturbation. Comp shock now clean: coalition -3.2, only same-sign rows. (`budget_frontier.py` had the same latent order-dependence, patched there only by non-monotone clamping; apply `_sm` there too if its per-topic deltas ever matter; done later in HIGH-1.)
s10.why: "below the MC noise floor" is a magnitude and "done later in HIGH-1" is time

s10.old: - **H3 (FIXED, later REVERSED)**: members with NO FEC data had ind = 0, b about 0, pflip about 1 ("missing" misread as "no industry opposition"); 11 of 63 ranked top-50 winnability, inflating the base (215.92). Fix: impute industry baseline (median of members WITH data) for zero-`total` members in `flip_model.py` + `per_topic_flip.py`; `fm.nodata` flags them. Base now realistic 186.50; 0 data-less in top-20. CAUGHT a follow-on: the scenario flip channel mixed imputed `fm.ind0` (baseline) with raw local `ind` (scenario), so the comp shock showed +28 winnability; fixed via `ind_flip = fm.ind0 + (ind-ind0_raw)` (one footing).
s10.why: "(FIXED, later REVERSED)" is time

s10.old: - **HIGH-3 (FIXED then reversed below)**: the H3 imputation only fired for total = 0; 43 members had a FEC record but ind = 0 (zero captured bank/finserv), 6 ranked top-20 winnability. Extended imputation to EVERY ind = 0 member (median industry money), `ind_imputed` set, env-tunable IMPUTE_IND0=0 to trust raw zeros. Conservative (only lowers inflated winnability). Base winnability 171.76 to 154.57.
